# Hermes 🕊️

> **Hermes** (the Greek messenger god): A lightweight blog and RSS/Atom/JSON feed monitor that delivers instant push notifications to your phone via [ntfy.sh](https://ntfy.sh), running entirely on GitHub Actions with zero server infrastructure.

---

## Architecture

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  GitHub Actions Runner (triggered every 15 minutes via cron) │
│                                                              │
│  Workflow: check-feeds.yml                                   │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │ 1. Checkout repo (includes seen.json state)            │  │
│  │ 2. Install dependencies (feedparser, requests, pyyaml) │  │
│  │ 3. Run hermes.py                                       │  │
│  │    ├── Load feeds.yaml & seen.json                     │  │
│  │    ├── Check feeds & detect new articles               │  │
│  │    ├── Send ntfy.sh push notification for new articles │  │
│  │    └── Prune articles older than 30 days               │  │
│  │ 4. Commit & push updated seen.json (only if changed)   │  │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
         │                              │
         ▼                              ▼
  ┌─────────────┐              ┌────────────────┐
  │  Blog Feeds │              │    ntfy.sh     │
  │ (RSS / Atom │              │  ───► Phone    │
  │  JSON Feed) │              │   Notification │
  └─────────────┘              └────────────────┘
```

---

## Setup Guide

### 1. Install the ntfy Mobile App

Download the free, open-source ntfy app for your device:
- **Android**: [ntfy on Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=io.heckel.ntfy) or [F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/en/packages/io.heckel.ntfy/)
- **iOS**: [ntfy on App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/ntfy/id1625396347)
- **Web**: Open [ntfy.sh](https://ntfy.sh) in any browser.

In the app, subscribe to a unique topic name of your choice (e.g. `hermes-myname-7f3b`).

### 2. Configure `feeds.yaml`

Edit `feeds.yaml` in the root of the repository:

```yaml
# Your private/unique ntfy topic
ntfy_topic: "hermes-myname-7f3b"

# Optional: self-hosted ntfy server (defaults to https://ntfy.sh)
# ntfy_server: "https://ntfy.sh"

# Optional: state retention window in days (defaults to 30)
# max_age_days: 30

# List of feeds to monitor
feeds:
  - name: "Julia Evans"
    url: "https://jvns.ca/atom.xml"

  - name: "Simon Willison"
    url: "https://simonwillison.net/atom/everything/"

  - name: "Dan Luu"
    url: "https://danluu.com/atom.xml"
```

### 3. Configure GitHub Workflow Permissions

Because Hermes commits state back to `seen.json`, your GitHub repository needs write permissions for workflows:
1. Go to your GitHub repository **Settings** → **Actions** → **General**.
2. Scroll to **Workflow permissions**.
3. Select **Read and write permissions**.
4. Click **Save**.

### 4. Optional: Private/Authenticated ntfy Topics

If using an authenticated ntfy topic or self-hosted instance with access control:
1. Go to repository **Settings** → **Secrets and variables** → **Actions**.
2. Create a new repository secret named `NTFY_TOKEN`.
3. Paste your token.

### 5. Seed Initial State & Test

1. Push your changes to GitHub.
2. In your repo, go to the **Actions** tab.
3. Select **Hermes Feed Checker** → **Run workflow**.
4. On the **first run**, Hermes marks all existing articles in your feeds as "seen" without spamming your phone.
5. On subsequent cron runs (every 15 minutes), any newly published articles will trigger a push notification.

---

## Notification Appearance

When a new article is detected, you will receive a notification formatted like:

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 📰 Julia Evans                       │
│                                      │
│ How DNS Works                        │
│                                      │
│ Tap to open article                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Title**: Blog name
- **Body**: Article title
- **Click**: Tapping opens the direct article URL in your browser.
- **Icon**: 📰 (`newspaper` tag)

---

## Git Log Hygiene

To filter out bot commits when reviewing repository history:

```bash
# Show only human commits
git log --oneline --invert-grep --grep="chore: update seen articles"

# Show only Hermes bot state update commits
git log --oneline --grep="chore: update seen articles"
```

---

## Local Development & Testing

```bash
# Create virtual environment
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Run tests
pytest tests/ -v

# Run Hermes locally
python hermes.py
```

26: ## Overview
27: 
28: **Goal**: Monitor a user-configured list of blogs (via their RSS, Atom, or JSON feeds) on a cron schedule, and send a push notification to the user's phone for every new article detected.
29: 
30: **Key Design Decisions** (already agreed upon):
31: 
32: | Decision | Choice |
33: |---|---|
34: | Language | Python 3 |
35: | Feed parsing | `feedparser` library |
36: | Notification delivery | ntfy.sh (free, HTTP-based push notification service) |
37: | Scheduling & runtime | GitHub Actions with `schedule` (cron) trigger |
38: | State persistence | JSON file committed to the repository |
39: | Configuration format | YAML file in the repository root |

138: ### 2. `seen.json` — State File
139: 
140: Tracks which articles have already triggered a notification. Committed to the repo automatically by the workflow.
141: 
142: **Schema:**
143: 
144: ```json
145: {
146:   "articles": {
147:     "https://jvns.ca/blog/2024/some-post/": 1691234567,
148:     "https://simonwillison.net/2024/some-post/": 1691234890
149:   }
150: }
151: ```
152: 
153: - **Key**: The article's unique identifier (see [Article Identity Resolution](#article-identity-resolution) below).
154: - **Value**: Unix timestamp of when the article was first seen. Used for pruning old entries.
155: 
156: **Pruning rule**: On every run, discard entries older than **30 days**. This keeps the file small and bounded. No blog feed contains entries older than 30 days anyway.
157: 
158: **Initial state**: The file should ship as `{"articles": {}}` in the repo. On the very first run, `hermes.py` must treat all current feed entries as "already seen" and add them to `seen.json` *without* sending notifications. This prevents a flood of notifications for old articles on first setup.
159: 
160: > [!IMPORTANT]
161: > **First-run behavior**: Detect first run by checking if `seen.json` contains an empty `articles` object. If empty, populate it with all current feed entry IDs but **do not send any notifications**. Only send notifications on subsequent runs for entries that are truly new.

165: ### 3. `hermes.py` — Core Script
166: 
167: The main Python script. Should be a single file, no classes needed — just clean procedural code with well-named functions.
168: 
169: #### Dependencies
170: 
171: - `feedparser` — Parses RSS, Atom, and JSON Feed formats with a single `feedparser.parse(url)` call.
172: - `requests` — For sending HTTP POST requests to ntfy.sh.
173: - `pyyaml` — For reading `feeds.yaml`.
174: - Standard library: `json`, `time`, `sys`, `pathlib`.
175: 
176: #### Main Flow (pseudocode)
177: 
178: ```
179: function main():
180:     config = load_yaml("feeds.yaml")
181:     seen = load_json("seen.json")
182:     is_first_run = (seen.articles is empty)
183: 
184:     new_count = 0
185: 
186:     for feed in config.feeds:
187:         entries = feedparser.parse(feed.url).entries
188: 
189:         for entry in entries:
190:             article_id = resolve_id(entry)
191: 
192:             if article_id not in seen.articles:
193:                 if not is_first_run:
194:                     send_notification(config, feed.name, entry)
195:                     new_count += 1
196:                 seen.articles[article_id] = current_unix_timestamp()
197: 
198:     prune_old_entries(seen, max_age_days=30)
199:     save_json("seen.json", seen)
200: 
201:     print(f"Found {new_count} new articles.")
202:     exit(0)
203: ```
204: 
205: #### Article Identity Resolution
206: 
207: `feedparser` normalizes entries from all feed formats. Use the following priority to determine a unique ID for each entry:
208: 
209: ```
210: 1. entry.id        (the <guid> in RSS, <id> in Atom)  — preferred
211: 2. entry.link      (the permalink URL)                 — fallback
212: 3. entry.title     (the article title)                 — last resort
213: ```
214: 
215: Always strip whitespace and normalize the ID. Implement this as a `resolve_id(entry)` function.
216: 
217: #### Error Handling
218: 
219: - **Feed fetch failure** (network error, 404, timeout): Log a warning to stderr and **skip that feed**. Do not crash the entire run because one blog is down. Use a try/except around each feed's processing.
220: - **ntfy.sh POST failure**: Log a warning to stderr and **continue**. The article will still be marked as seen (to avoid duplicate notifications on retry). This is a deliberate trade-off — missing one notification is better than getting duplicates.
221: - **Malformed feed** (feedparser returns bozo=True with no entries): Log a warning and skip.
222: - **Missing `feeds.yaml`**: Exit with a clear error message and non-zero exit code.
223: - **Missing `seen.json`**: Treat as first run (create it with empty articles).
224: 
225: #### Logging
226: 
227: Use `print()` to stdout for normal operation messages:
228: - `"Checking feed: {name} ({url})"`
229: - `"New article: {title}"`
230: - `"Found {n} new articles across {m} feeds."`
231: 
232: Use `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` for warnings/errors:
233: - `"Warning: Failed to fetch feed '{name}': {error}"`
234: - `"Warning: Failed to send notification for '{title}': {error}"`
235: 
236: Do **not** use the `logging` module — it's overkill for a script this small.

314: ## Detailed Behavior & Edge Cases
315: 
316: ### Article Identity Resolution — expanded
317: 
318: | Feed Type | `entry.id` value | `entry.link` value |
319: |---|---|---|
320: | RSS with `<guid>` | The GUID string (often a URL) | Permalink URL |
321: | RSS without `<guid>` | `None` | Permalink URL |
322: | Atom | The `<id>` element (usually a URN or URL) | Permalink URL |
323: | JSON Feed | The `id` field | The `url` field |
324: 
325: `feedparser` normalizes all of these into `entry.id` and `entry.link`.
326: 
327: ### What if a blog changes its feed URL?
328: 
329: The user updates `feeds.yaml`. Old seen entries (keyed by article ID, not feed URL) are still in `seen.json`, so no duplicate notifications are sent — article IDs are typically stable across feed URL changes.
330: 
331: ### What if `seen.json` gets corrupted?
332: 
333: If `seen.json` is not valid JSON, treat it as a first run (log a warning, rebuild from scratch, don't notify). This is the safest recovery path.
334: 
335: ### What if feedparser can't determine any ID?
336: 
337: If `entry.id`, `entry.link`, and `entry.title` are all missing/empty, skip that entry and log a warning. This should essentially never happen with real-world feeds.

341: ## ntfy.sh Integration Details
342: 
343: ntfy.sh is a simple HTTP-based pub/sub notification service. No API key is required for basic usage.
344: 
345: ### Sending a Notification
346: 
347: ```
348: POST https://ntfy.sh/{topic}
349: Headers:
350:   Title: {blog_name}: {article_title}
351:   Click: {article_url}
352:   Tags: newspaper
353: 
354: Body: {article_title}
355: ```
356: 
357: **Implementation as a function:**
358: 
359: ```python
360: def send_notification(config, blog_name, entry):
361:     topic = config["ntfy_topic"]
362:     server = config.get("ntfy_server", "https://ntfy.sh")
363:     url = f"{server}/{topic}"
364: 
365:     title = entry.get("title", "New article")
366:     link = entry.get("link", "")
367: 
368:     headers = {
369:         "Title": f"{blog_name}: {title}",
370:         "Tags": "newspaper",
371:     }
372:     if link:
373:         headers["Click"] = link
374: 
375:     requests.post(url, data=title.encode("utf-8"), headers=headers, timeout=10)
376: ```
377: 
378: **What the user sees on their phone:**
379: 
380: ```
381: ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
382: │ 📰 Julia Evans: How DNS Works      │
383: │                                     │
384: │ How DNS Works                       │
385: │                                     │
386: │ Tap to open article                 │
387: └─────────────────────────────────────┘
388: ```
389: 
390: - The `Title` header sets the notification title.
391: - The `Click` header makes tapping the notification open the article URL in the browser.
392: - The `Tags: newspaper` header adds a 📰 emoji icon to the notification.
393: 
394: ### ntfy.sh Authentication (optional)
395: 
396: If the user wants to use a private/authenticated ntfy topic (to prevent others from posting to it), they can:
397: 
398: 1. Set up access control on ntfy.sh.
399: 2. Store the ntfy token as a GitHub Actions secret named `NTFY_TOKEN`.
400: 3. Pass it to the script via an environment variable.
401: 4. Add an `Authorization: Bearer {token}` header to the POST request.
402: 
403: This is optional. For most personal use, an obscure topic name (e.g., `hermes-a7f3b2c9`) is sufficient.
404: 
405: If implementing, add this to the workflow:
406: 
407: ```yaml
408: - name: Run Hermes
409:   run: python hermes.py
410:   env:
411:     NTFY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NTFY_TOKEN }}
412: ```
413: 
414: And in `hermes.py`, check `os.environ.get("NTFY_TOKEN")` and add the auth header if present.

# 🌐 Hermes Web Dashboard — Implementation Plan

> A static HTML dashboard generated on each GitHub Actions run and deployed to GitHub Pages, giving at-a-glance visibility into feed health and recent articles.

---

## Overview

The dashboard is a **single self-contained `index.html` file** (no build tools, no JS frameworks) generated by a Python script during the existing Actions workflow. It reads the two JSON data sources already committed to the repo and produces a static page deployed to GitHub Pages via the `gh-pages` branch.

```
feed-status.json ──┐
                    ├──► generate_dashboard.py ──► docs/index.html ──► GitHub Pages
seen.json ─────────┘
```

---

## Data Sources (already exist — no changes needed)

### [`feed-status.json`](file:///Users/jaikumardewani/Projects/Hermes/feed-status.json)
Primary data source. Per-feed health metrics with stable schema:
```json
{
  "last_updated": "2026-10-03T16:43:34Z",
  "feeds": {
    "Julia Evans (Linux/OS)": {
      "url": "https://jvns.ca/atom.xml",
      "article_count": 20,
      "last_success": "2026-10-03T16:43:29Z",
      "last_error": null,
      "consecutive_failures": 0
    }
  }
}
```

### [`seen.json`](file:///Users/jaikumardewani/Projects/Hermes/seen.json)
Article state (rolling 30-day window):
```json
{
  "articles": {
    "<article_id>": {
      "first_seen": 1789328908,
      "title": "How DNS Works",
      "link": "https://jvns.ca/blog/2024/how-dns-works/",
      "blog_name": "Julia Evans (Linux/OS)"
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Proposed File Layout

```
hermes/
├── lib/
│   └── dashboard.py          # NEW — generate_dashboard() function
├── docs/
│   └── index.html            # NEW — generated output (gitignored? see Decision 1)
├── .github/
│   └── workflows/
│       └── check-feeds.yml   # MODIFIED — add dashboard generation + Pages deploy steps
└── hermes.py                 # MODIFIED — call generate_dashboard() at the end of main()
```

---

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Create `lib/dashboard.py`

A single function `generate_dashboard(feed_status, seen, output_path)` that:

1. **Reads** the in-memory `feed_status` and `seen` dicts (already loaded in `main()`)
2. **Renders** a self-contained HTML string using Python `string.Template` or f-strings (no Jinja dependency)
3. **Writes** the HTML to `output_path` (e.g., `docs/index.html`)

The HTML will contain three sections:

#### Section A — Feed Health Status Table
Source: `feed-status.json`

| Column | Source Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Feed Name | dict key | Sortable |
| Feed URL | `url` | Clickable link |
| Status | derived | ✅ OK / ⚠️ Flaky (1–2 failures) / ❌ Down (3+ failures) |
| Articles Tracked | `article_count` | Count from last successful fetch |
| Last Success | `last_success` | Relative time (e.g., "2 hours ago") via JS |
| Last Error | `last_error` | Truncated, shown in a `<details>` expandable if long |
| Consecutive Failures | `consecutive_failures` | Highlighted red if > 0 |

#### Section B — Recent Articles Timeline
Source: `seen.json`

- Sorted by `first_seen` descending (newest first)
- Capped at **50 most recent** articles (keeps page lightweight)
- Each entry shows:
  - Blog name (color-coded badge)
  - Article title (clickable link)
  - Relative timestamp ("3 hours ago", "2 days ago")
- Grouped by day (date headers: "Today", "Yesterday", "Oct 1, 2026")

#### Section C — Article Counts Per Blog
Source: `seen.json` (aggregate by `blog_name`)

- Horizontal bar chart or simple ranked table
- Shows total tracked articles per blog within the 30-day window
- Sorted descending by count

#### Page Design

- Self-contained: all CSS inline (no external stylesheets or CDN)
- Minimal JS: only for relative timestamps (`<time>` elements + small script)
- Dark/light mode: respects `prefers-color-scheme`
- Responsive: works on mobile
- Header: "🕊️ Hermes Dashboard" + "Last updated: {timestamp}"
- Footer: "Generated by [Hermes](repo-link) • Auto-refreshes every 15 minutes"

### Step 2: Integrate into `hermes.py`

Add a call at the end of `main()`, after saving state files:

```python
from lib.dashboard import generate_dashboard

# ... existing code ...

# Generate dashboard
generate_dashboard(feed_status, seen, "docs/index.html")
print("Dashboard generated: docs/index.html")
```

### Step 3: Update GitHub Actions workflow

# 🌐 Hermes Web Dashboard — Implementation Plan (v2)

> A static HTML dashboard generated by a **separate GitHub Actions workflow**, triggered on each successful feed-check run, and deployed to GitHub Pages.

---

## Overview

```
data/feed-status.json ──┐
                         ├──► generate_dashboard.py ──► docs/index.html ──► GitHub Pages
data/seen.json ──────────┘
```

Two key structural changes from v1:
1. **`data/` folder** — `seen.json` and `feed-status.json` move from the repo root into `data/`
2. **Separate workflow** — dashboard generation lives in its own `deploy-dashboard.yml`, triggered automatically via `workflow_run` when `check-feeds.yml` completes successfully

---

## Data Sources (existing files, moving to `data/`)

### `data/feed-status.json` (currently [`feed-status.json`](file:///Users/jaikumardewani/Projects/Hermes/feed-status.json))
Primary dashboard data source. Per-feed health metrics:
```json
{
  "last_updated": "2026-10-03T16:43:34Z",
  "feeds": {
    "Julia Evans (Linux/OS)": {
      "url": "https://jvns.ca/atom.xml",
      "article_count": 20,
      "last_success": "2026-10-03T16:43:29Z",
      "last_error": null,
      "consecutive_failures": 0
    }
  }
}
```

### `data/seen.json` (currently [`seen.json`](file:///Users/jaikumardewani/Projects/Hermes/seen.json))
Article state (rolling 30-day window):
```json
{
  "articles": {
    "<article_id>": {
      "first_seen": 1789328908,
      "title": "How DNS Works",
      "link": "https://jvns.ca/blog/2024/how-dns-works/",
      "blog_name": "Julia Evans (Linux/OS)"
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Proposed File Layout

```diff
 hermes/
 ├── .github/
 │   └── workflows/
-│       └── check-feeds.yml        # MODIFIED — paths updated to data/
+│       ├── check-feeds.yml        # MODIFIED — paths updated to data/
+│       └── deploy-dashboard.yml   # NEW — triggered by check-feeds success
+├── data/
+│   ├── seen.json                  # MOVED from repo root
+│   └── feed-status.json           # MOVED from repo root
 ├── lib/
+│   ├── dashboard.py               # NEW — generate_dashboard() function
 │   ├── config.py
 │   ├── feed.py
 │   ├── notify.py
 │   ├── state.py                   # MODIFIED — default paths → data/
 │   └── summary.py
+├── docs/
+│   └── index.html                 # NEW — generated dashboard output
 ├── hermes.py                      # MODIFIED — call generate_dashboard()
 └── tests/
     ├── test_hermes.py             # MODIFIED — paths updated to data/
+    └── test_dashboard.py          # NEW
```

---

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Move JSON files into `data/`

Move `seen.json` → `data/seen.json` and `feed-status.json` → `data/feed-status.json`.

Files that need path updates:

| File | What changes |
|---|---|
| [`hermes.py`](file:///Users/jaikumardewani/Projects/Hermes/hermes.py) | `load_seen("data/seen.json")`, `load_feed_status("data/feed-status.json")`, `save_seen("data/seen.json", ...)`, `save_feed_status("data/feed-status.json", ...)` |
| [`lib/state.py`](file:///Users/jaikumardewani/Projects/Hermes/lib/state.py) | Default parameter values: `"seen.json"` → `"data/seen.json"`, `"feed-status.json"` → `"data/feed-status.json"` |
| [`check-feeds.yml`](file:///Users/jaikumardewani/Projects/Hermes/.github/workflows/check-feeds.yml) | `git add data/seen.json data/feed-status.json` |
| [`tests/test_hermes.py`](file:///Users/jaikumardewani/Projects/Hermes/tests/test_hermes.py) | Any hardcoded paths to the JSON files |
| [`.gitignore`](file:///Users/jaikumardewani/Projects/Hermes/.gitignore) | Ensure `data/` is **not** gitignored |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Use `git mv` to preserve history: `git mv seen.json data/seen.json && git mv feed-status.json data/feed-status.json`

---

### Step 2: Create `lib/dashboard.py`

A single function `generate_dashboard(feed_status, seen, output_path)` that:

1. **Receives** the in-memory `feed_status` and `seen` dicts (already loaded in `main()`)
2. **Renders** a self-contained HTML string using Python `string.Template` or f-strings (no Jinja — no new dependency)
3. **Writes** the HTML to `output_path` (e.g., `docs/index.html`)

#### Section A — Feed Health Status Table
Source: `data/feed-status.json`

| Column | Source Field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Feed Name | dict key | Sortable |
| Feed URL | `url` | Clickable link |
| Status | derived | ✅ OK / ⚠️ Flaky (1–2 failures) / ❌ Down (3+ failures) |
| Articles Tracked | `article_count` | Count from last successful fetch |
| Last Success | `last_success` | Relative time via small inline JS |
| Last Error | `last_error` | Truncated, expandable via `<details>` |
| Consecutive Failures | `consecutive_failures` | Highlighted red if > 0 |

#### Section B — Recent Articles Timeline
Source: `data/seen.json`

- Sorted by `first_seen` descending (newest first)
- Capped at **50 most recent** articles
- Each entry: blog name badge + clickable article title + relative timestamp
- Grouped by day ("Today", "Yesterday", "Oct 1, 2026")

#### Section C — Article Counts Per Blog
Source: `data/seen.json` (aggregate by `blog_name`)

- Ranked table or inline CSS bar chart
- Total tracked articles per blog within the 30-day window
- Sorted descending by count

#### Page Design
- Self-contained: all CSS inline, no external stylesheets or CDN
- Minimal JS: only for relative timestamps
- Dark/light mode: respects `prefers-color-scheme`
- Responsive: works on mobile
- Header: "🕊️ Hermes Dashboard" + "Last updated: {timestamp}"
- Footer: "Generated by Hermes • Auto-refreshes every 15 minutes"

---

### Step 3: Integrate into `hermes.py`

Add a call at the end of `main()`, after saving state files:

```python
from lib.dashboard import generate_dashboard

# ... after save_seen() and save_feed_status() ...
generate_dashboard(feed_status, seen, "docs/index.html")
print("Dashboard generated: docs/index.html")
```

---

### Step 4: Update `check-feeds.yml`

Two changes to the existing workflow:

```yaml
# 1. Update git add paths
- name: Commit updated state
  run: |
    git config user.name "hermes-bot"
    git config user.email "hermes-bot@users.noreply.github.com"
    git add data/seen.json data/feed-status.json docs/index.html
    git diff --cached --quiet || git commit -m "chore: update seen articles"
    git push
```

> [!NOTE]
> `docs/index.html` is committed to `main` alongside the data files. The separate dashboard workflow then deploys it to GitHub Pages.

---

### Step 5: Create `deploy-dashboard.yml`

A new workflow triggered by the successful completion of `check-feeds.yml`:

```yaml
name: Deploy Dashboard

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["Hermes Feed Checker"]   # must match the `name:` in check-feeds.yml
    types: [completed]

permissions:
  pages: write
  id-token: write

# Only deploy if the triggering run succeeded
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}

    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      - name: Upload dashboard artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: docs/

      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
```

**Why this design:**
- `workflow_run` with `types: [completed]` + the `if: conclusion == 'success'` guard ensures the dashboard is only deployed after a successful feed check — never after a failed run
- The dashboard workflow has its own permissions (`pages: write`, `id-token: write`) — no need to bloat `check-feeds.yml` with Pages permissions
- Each workflow has a single clear responsibility

**One-time setup required:**
1. Go to repo **Settings → Pages**
2. Set source to **GitHub Actions** (not "Deploy from a branch")

---

### Step 6: Add tests

New file `tests/test_dashboard.py`:

| Test | What it verifies |
|---|---|
| `test_generate_dashboard_creates_file` | Output file is created at the specified path |
| `test_dashboard_contains_feed_names` | All feed names from status data appear in the HTML |
| `test_dashboard_contains_recent_articles` | Recent article titles appear in the HTML |
| `test_dashboard_article_count_per_blog` | Per-blog counts are correctly aggregated |
| `test_dashboard_status_icons` | ✅/⚠️/❌ assigned correctly based on `consecutive_failures` |
| `test_dashboard_empty_data` | Handles empty dicts gracefully (no crash, shows "no data" message) |
| `test_dashboard_caps_at_50_articles` | Timeline section doesn't exceed 50 entries |

---

### Step 7: Update documentation

- **[`TECHNICAL.md`](file:///Users/jaikumardewani/Projects/Hermes/TECHNICAL.md)**: Move dashboard from "Planned" → "Completed" in roadmap; add component deep-dive for `lib/dashboard.py` and `deploy-dashboard.yml`; update repo structure tree
- **[`README.md`](file:///Users/jaikumardewani/Projects/Hermes/README.md)**: Add "Dashboard" section with GitHub Pages URL; update repo structure
- Both docs: reflect the `data/` folder move in all file trees and references

---

## Open Decisions

> [!IMPORTANT]
> These need your input before implementation begins.

### Decision 1: Article counts visualization
**Option A** — Simple ranked HTML table (zero JS, fastest to build)
**Option B** — Inline CSS bar chart (visually richer, still no external deps)

### Decision 2: Should dashboard generation be opt-in?
- **Always generate** (default — no config change needed)?
- Or add a `dashboard: true` toggle in `feeds.yaml`?

### Decision 3: Scope of first iteration
Ship all three sections (health table + timeline + counts) in one go, or start with just the feed health table and iterate?

---

## Estimated Effort

| Component | Estimate |
|---|---|
| `data/` migration (move files + update paths) | ~15–20 lines changed |
| `lib/dashboard.py` (HTML generation) | ~150–200 lines |
| `hermes.py` integration | ~5 lines |
| `check-feeds.yml` updates | ~5 lines |
| `deploy-dashboard.yml` (new workflow) | ~35 lines |
| `tests/test_dashboard.py` | ~80–100 lines |
| Documentation updates | ~40 lines |
| **Total** | **~350–420 lines of new/modified code** |

---

## Dependencies

- **No new Python packages** — `string.Template`, `json`, `datetime`, `pathlib` (all stdlib)
- **No frontend build tools** — pure HTML/CSS + small inline `<script>` for relative timestamps
- **GitHub Pages** — free for public repos; one-time setup in Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions
- **New Actions used**: `actions/configure-pages@v5`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3`, `actions/deploy-pages@v4`
